name: The Davis household at the Steamboat Hotel
head: davis_john

arrival.note: NOT ATTESTED. He is documented in the town in 1835 and nothing dates his coming. The value is the earliest year the evidence forces and it is graded conjectural; the attested fact is in present_on_scene_date, not here.

lives_at.note: A keeper lived in his house; not stated.

present_on_scene_date.note: Named as the keeper in the scene year and replaced only in November 1835.

persons.name: John Davis

occupation.note: Keeper of the Steamboat Hotel on North Water Street. Andreas's list of the Chicago American's advertising patrons in the paper's first year carries 'John Davis, Steamboat Hotel'.

persons.note: DOCUMENTED IN THE SCENE YEAR ITSELF: the American began in June 1835 and he is advertising in it. The hotel chronology has J. Dorsey and J. Force taking over the management on 9 November 1835, so his tenure covers 1 July. A COINCIDENCE THIS PROJECT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT RESOLVE: a 'Mr. Davis' also took over the Sauganash Hotel in 1835, and whether that is this man is unknown. If it is, one household kept two houses; if it is not, there is a second Davis in the town. Nothing reached settles it and neither reading is asserted here.

research_note: A HOUSEHOLD WHOSE ONLY DOCUMENTED FACT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS - that a man of this name was keeping this house in the scene year. Everything else about him is blank, and four of the five household fields are conjectural as a result. THE SAUGANASH QUESTION IS LEFT OPEN ON PURPOSE. data/structures/sauganash_hotel.json records 'a Mr. Davis, proprietor' for 1835 and flags the possibility that he is this man; merging the two would create a documented claim out of a shared surname, and splitting them would create a second household out of the same. Neither is done.
